nodes.label: Transport contract (M1 SP8)
nodes.rationale: Scope per spec section 9: HttpTransportPort, direct branch and timeout only; relay, proxy pools, outbound proxy and MITM-bypass DNS sit behind the same port later (SP18). SP8 has no HTTP API and no UI.

nodes.label: HttpTransportPort
HttpRequest (requires timeoutMs)
HttpResponse
readBoundedText() (bounded body reader, default 4 MiB)
nodes.rationale: A body over maxBytes cancels the stream and throws; a truncated body is never returned.

nodes.label: DirectTransport (direct branch implementation)
nodes.rationale: https only (http to loopback only), timeoutMs inside ctx.signal covering headers and body, never follows redirects, caller abort keeps its reason, errors name the host only.

nodes.label: TransportModule (injects DirectTransport under HTTP_TRANSPORT)
Bounded context: transport
transport.proxy-priority-chain
nodes.rationale: REFERENCE_BEHAVIOR: with no relay and no proxy, 9router sends to the unpatched global fetch. Kept as the direct branch; contracted because relay and proxy branches come in SP18.

nodes.label: Rule: every call states timeoutMs (1 to 600000 ms), bounding headers and body inside ctx.signal
nodes.rationale: 9router fallback.timeout: null means the direct chat fetch had no timeout, labeled IMPLEMENTATION_ACCIDENT; spec section 4.2 requires the shared ctx.signal deadline.

nodes.label: Rule: error messages and details name the host only; headers (Authorization) never appear
Failure: malformed URL or non-https (http only to localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1])
Failure: timeoutMs not an integer from 1 to 600000
Failure: caller ctx.signal aborts (client left, budget spent)
nodes.result: Rejects with ctx.signal.reason unchanged, never relabeled as a provider failure

nodes.label: Failure: no headers or stalled body within timeoutMs
Failure: connection refused, DNS failure, TLS failure
Failure: upstream answers 3xx (redirect not followed)
nodes.rationale: Not following the redirect keeps the credential from going to another host.

nodes.label: Upstream answers 4xx or 5xx
nodes.result: Returned as a normal HttpResponse; the adapter classifies the status (SP9)

nodes.label: Failure: body larger than maxBytes in readBoundedText
nodes.result: Stream cancelled, EngineError PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE; truncated body never returned

nodes.label: Lint rule aigate/fetch-through-transport
nodes.rationale: Spec section 4.2 / SP0.1: raw fetch with an opaque signal stayed rejected until a bounded helper existed; the transport is that helper, so fetch is rejected in server and packages except modules/transport/infrastructure/.

nodes.label: Lint rule aigate/retry-through-helper
nodes.rationale: Spec section 11.2: no uncapped retry, only through the single helper. A loop around an awaited try/catch in server or engine is rejected (retry.ts exempt); use withRetry.

nodes.label: Lint rule aigate/fetch-timeout (accepts AbortSignal.any([..., AbortSignal.timeout(n)]))
tools/lint/check.test.mjs (lint:check 13/13)
apps/server/test/transport.test.mjs (10 tests, real local HTTP server, 6 mutations caught)
nodes.rationale: Mutations caught: following redirects, relabeling a caller abort, dropping the per-request timeout, allowing http to any host, returning the raw body without error mapping, an unbounded body read. Each test checks the credential is not in the error.

nodes.label: Rule: server, engine, and database test scripts pass --test-timeout=30000
nodes.rationale: The mutation that dropped the timeout hung the test run instead of failing it.

nodes.label: Deferred: streaming idle timeout (gap between chunks) with SP12
nodes.rationale: Until SP12, timeoutMs bounds the whole stream.

nodes.label: API_UI_MAP row: SP8 transport, No UI
nodes.rationale: Outbound HTTP only; its error codes (TIMEOUT, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, INVALID_REQUEST) reach users through /v1 in SP12.

nodes.label: API_UI_MAP row: SP7 packages/engine, No UI
nodes.rationale: No HTTP API; /v1 (SP12) is the first thing a screen can show.
